## Measured: the direction is fail-SOFT — but the obvious fix would CAUSE the bug, not fix it

⛔ **Nothing changed for this card.** Measurement only, taken while the app was booted for
#8990's browser round (PR #9280), which paid the expensive prerequisite. This finding is
still ungraded and unqueued.

### 1. Direction: fail-SOFT confirmed — an unevaluable predicate leaves the banner VISIBLE

`RecordAlertRenderer` (`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx`) evaluates
its gate as `useCondition(toPredicateInput(props.visible), { record })` — **without**
`throwOnError`. That is the fail-soft posture on both paths, and `ActionEngine` documents
why in its own comment for the opposite choice:

> `throwOnError: true` is required for fail-closed semantics: the evaluator's default
> behavior swallows expression errors and returns the raw template string, which
> `Boolean(string)` then coerces to `true` … It is equally load-bearing on the CEL path,
> where the canonical helper fails SOFT to visible/enabled unless the caller opts in.

So objectui#4807's reading is right, and it is the opposite of the action face:
**a faulting `record:alert` predicate shows the banner to everyone.** On `sys_user` that
is "Email not verified" in front of verified users.

### 2. But the absent-key half never fires on a record-detail page — this is the crux

The PM's mechanism assumption 4 ("a detail read may project every declared column") is
**CONFIRMED**, measured against the running app rather than reasoned:

```
GET /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo            (no $select — the detail read)
  Specimen — Full     59 keys returned, 15 of them holding null
  Specimen — Minimal  59 keys returned, 37 of them holding null

GET /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo?$select=<the 5 default-list columns>
  both rows           exactly 5 keys returned — nothing else, not even id
```

A detail read returns **every declared column**, with nulls materialised as present keys
holding null. Evaluating all 53 showcase action predicates against those real payloads:
**40 of 53 fault on a list row, 0 of 53 fault on a detail record.**

`record:alert` only ever renders inside a record-detail context. So the absent-key fault —
the one that would make the banner permanently visible — **does not occur today** on a
normally-loaded detail page. The renderer also already hides while `record` is unloaded,
covering the empty first frame. That lowers this finding's severity considerably.

### 3. ⚠️ The counterintuitive part: applying #8990's guard here would CREATE the bug

Page-block predicates do **not** go through `defineAction`'s normalization. Measured in the
built artifact — of 114 record-scoped `visible`/`disabled` values in
`examples/app-showcase/dist/objectstack.json`, **113 are `{dialect:'cel', source}`
envelopes and exactly one is a bare string**:

```
BARE STRING at pages/15/regions/0/components/1/properties
   visible = "record.status == 'in_review'"      ← task-detail.page.ts:51, this card
```

`toPredicateInput` keeps a `cel` envelope routed to `@objectstack/formula`, but wraps a
bare string as `${…}` for **objectui's legacy JS evaluator** — and that evaluator has no
`has()`. Run directly against `SafeExpressionParser` at the pinned objectui sha
(`665661ab`):

```
record.status == "in_review"                          => true
has(record.status) && record.status == "in_review"    => THREW TypeError: "has" is not a function
record.email_verified == false                        => true
has(record.email_verified) && record.email_verified == false
                                                      => THREW TypeError: "has" is not a function
```

Combine that with §1: on this fail-soft surface a throw means **visible**. So mechanically
applying #8990's action-face guard to these two predicates would turn a banner that is
currently correct into one that is **permanently visible for every user** — precisely the
bug this card was filed to worry about, newly created by its own fix.

### What that implies for grading

The defect is real but **latent, not live**: it needs a detail read that does not project
the column (a partial/deferred read, an embedded card, a custom page passing a projected
record), not the ordinary path. And the fix is **not** "add `has()`":

- either the page-block `visible` must be normalized into a `{dialect:'cel'}` envelope at
  build time, the way `defineAction` already does — after which `has()` works and the
  action-face guard applies unchanged;
- or the `record:alert` gate must opt into `throwOnError` and choose a deliberate
  direction, which is a behaviour change objectui owns;
- or both, in that order.

I did not pick between them and wrote no line for it. The first looks right to me
(one normalization, one dialect, the guard then means the same thing on every surface),
but it is a spec/build-surface decision, and the page-block face may have callers that
rely on the template dialect.

⚠️ One limit on the above: this session had **no browser tooling**, so §1's direction is
read off the pinned objectui source and its own documented contract, not observed as a
rendered banner. §2 and §3 are direct measurements against the running server and the
built artifact.

## ⚠️ Read this before acting on the struck steps

Steps 2 and 3 of "What is owed" are struck with ⛔ because a 2026-08-20 browser round measured them **harmful** — applying `has()` guards turned two correctly-hidden banners into permanently-visible ones.

**That measurement was taken under pre-binding physics.** At the time, node-level `visibleWhen` bound no `record` at all, so a `record.*` predicate could not resolve and fail-softed to visible. `c86185eb5` is precisely the commit that changed that. The strike may therefore be stale — but ⛔ **do not un-strike it on this comment's say-so.** Re-run the measurement first; the strike stands until something measures it false, and this card's whole history is a record of what reasoning-instead-of-measuring cost here.

Useful prior art for whoever takes it: objectui#5401's retrospective survey (comment `5380283415`) found **2** authored `record.*` sites reaching the node gate, **0** verdict changes from the binding — and the two sites it names are exactly this card's two predicates.

## Claim — dispatched as a **measurement**, not as an implementation

Seat `domain:engine` · session `session_01RfyXxZ2WPjcjhuXpiQQc3y` · branch `claude/issue-9167-record-alert-predicate-measurement`

**Why it is dispatchable now.** The unlock sweep released this card at 03:47:48 with **both halves of its two-part condition measured**, which I re-verified rather than took on trust: objectui#5401 closed, satisfied by objectui#5505 whose binding commit is `c86185eb5`; and `.objectui-sha` on `origin/main` is `190fbd01d0615e2e168faf9e08b8ad7844bc039d`, with `git merge-base --is-ancestor c86185eb5 190fbd01d` → **true**. I independently confirmed the pin value. Ancestry was measured, not inferred from dates — and the sweep flagged the shallow-checkout trap that makes the naive check answer "not a valid object" first.

Duplicate check run (the method that works here — repo-scoped PR search; ⛔ REST `/search/issues` is proxy-blocked and returns a **silent zero**, which is worse than not checking): no PR claims this card. The matches are #9280 / #9166, both about #8990, plus unrelated dependabot noise.

### ⛔ The deliverable is a reading, not a diff

The card says this itself and I am dispatching it exactly that way:

> the right first step is a measurement, not a rewrite: boot the real app, open a record-detail page whose read does not project the gated column, and see what the banner does

**Steps 2 and 3 of "What is owed" stay STRUCK.** They were measured on 2026-08-20 to break both banners — turning a correctly-hidden banner permanently visible, screenshot-confirmed on both pages.

⚠️ **And here is the subtlety that makes this card dangerous to hand to anyone mechanical**: that measurement was taken under **pre-binding physics**. At the time, node-level `visibleWhen` bound no `record` at all, so a `record.*` predicate could not resolve and fail-softed to visible. **`c86185eb5` is precisely the commit that changed that.** So the strike may now be stale — ⛔ **but it is not to be lifted on that reasoning.** The strike stands until something *measures* it false. This card's whole history is a record of what reasoning-instead-of-measuring cost.

### Two corrections carried into the brief so they are not re-inherited

1. **The card's own title is falsified.** "same sparse-face fault class as #8990" is **not true** of these two predicates: both are served as **bare strings**, so both run on objectui's legacy JS evaluator, where a missing key is `undefined` and `undefined == 'in_review'` is plain **`false`** — not a fault. The absent-key fault class does not reach this surface. What was found is real; what it was named is wrong.
2. **They are one case, not two.** An earlier PM note claimed `sys-user.page.ts:79` carried a `{dialect:'cel'}` envelope while only `task-detail.page.ts:51` was bare. That was wrong — it mis-attributed a count taken over `defineAction`-normalized *action* predicates in the built artifact. Measured three ways (authored source, built `dist`, served `/api/v1/meta/page`) the two are **identical on every dimension tested**. ⛔ Not to be re-inherited.

### Declared file surface — likely **none**

- `packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-user.page.ts:79` and `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/task-detail.page.ts:51` are the *subjects*, but a code change is an outcome this dispatch does **not** presume. A PR containing only a measurement report and a card update is a complete, successful result here.

### Tier: default. Not clause ②

Nothing changes contract accept/reject behaviour or widens a public surface — and if the measurement turns out to imply such a change, that is a **fork back to this card**, not a thing to absorb.

## Measurement round, 2026-08-23 — real console at objectui pin `190fbd01d`. No source change.

Dev seat `domain:engine`, session `session_01RfyXxZ2WPjcjhuXpiQQc3y`, branch `claude/issue-9167-record-alert-predicate-measurement`. **Zero lines written**: `git status --short` empty, `git diff origin/main...HEAD` empty, one empty commit `b08d89b59`. Every mutation below is a **network-response rewrite** against the shipped, unmodified console bundle — so each result is an observation of the pinned renderer, not of a tree I built. (PR #11245 was opened per the original brief and is closed again per the revised one; this comment is the durable artifact.)

### TL;DR — four readings, two of them reversing the previous round

1. ⛔ **The strike on steps 2–3 is NOT stale. It reproduces exactly at today's pin.** Applying a `has()` guard *in place* to `properties.visible` still turns a correctly-hidden banner into a permanently-visible one, on both pages, with `"has" is not a function` in the console (D1, D2). Screenshot-confirmed: "Email not verified" rendered directly above the page's own "Email Verified: ✓ Yes" chip. **Leave steps 2–3 struck.**
2. ⭐ **`record:alert` now honours the node-level `visibleWhen` gate** — the thing measured *inert* on 2026-08-20. `visibleWhen: {cel,'false'}` on the banner now HIDES it (E1), where the same probe did nothing before.
3. ⭐ **Node-level `visibleWhen` binds `record` and `ctx.user`**, polarity-correct on both pages (F1/F2, G4/G5/G6b) — `c86185eb5` observed working through the vendored bundle, not inferred from its title.
4. ✅ **The follow-up this card actually wants is now measured SAFE** — but only in the shape "move the predicate to `visibleWhen` (CEL) **and remove it from `properties.visible`**", with `has()` guards. Not applied: that is the PM's ruling, not mine.

### Environment

| what | value |
|:--|:--|
| framework | `origin/main` @ `281069522`, dedicated worktree, `turbo build` → `Tasks: 71 successful, 71 total` |
| console bundle | rebuilt from the repo's pin: `✓ @objectstack/console dist ready (49388 KB) from objectui@190fbd01d061`, with `✓ Bundle canary 'import/jobs' present` and `✓ Console bundle carries THIS tree's @objectstack/spec, and only it` |
| pin ancestry | verified **in this run**: `c86185eb5237a79d…` *"Bind `record` into node-level `visibleWhen`, and stop `visible` swallowing it (#5505)"*, Fri Aug 21 08:09:49 2026 — `git merge-base --is-ancestor c86185eb5 190fbd01d` → **true**. The clone is shallow and answers `Not a valid object name` first; re-run after `git fetch --depth=400`. |
| server | `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p 39167`, own sqlite file, 48 plugins, 132 seed rows |
| browser | Playwright 1.62.1 driving **chromium-1194** from `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` via an `executablePath` override (the bundled 1.62 expects build 1234; ⛔ `playwright install` was not run) |

### What the block binds today (question 1)

The console's detail read is `GET /api/v1/data/{object}?populate=…&top=1&filter=["id","=",{id}]` — **no `$select`** — and it projects everything:

| object | declared fields | keys returned | only absent declared field | nulls materialised as present keys |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|--:|
| `showcase_task` | 25 | 25 | `__search` | 9 |
| `sys_user` | 26 | 25 | `__search` | 9 |

Both gate fields (`status`, `email_verified`) are present, so the sparse case is not reachable on the ordinary path — it had to be **forced** by rewriting the response.

On the wire (`/api/v1/meta/page`, 34 pages served): **exactly 2 `record:alert` blocks exist**, this card's two, and **both carry `visible` as a bare string with no `visibleWhen`** — `showcase_task_detail` at `regions[0].components[1]`, `sys_user_detail` at `slots.alerts[0]`. Identical on every dimension tested; the "one is a `{dialect:'cel'}` envelope" claim stays falsified. Separately, all **6** authored `visibleWhen` values served are `{dialect:'cel'}` envelopes and **0** are bare — an author writing a bare string into `visibleWhen` gets CEL for free.

### Runs

Every "hidden" verdict is paired with a mount of the same shape that must SHOW; every run carries a page-render control; `metaPatched` / `keysRemoved` are interception counters proving the rewrite was live.

**Baselines — both banners are correct today (unmodified)**

| run | page / row | verdict | expected |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | task `in_review` | **VISIBLE** | VISIBLE ✅ |
| A2 | task `todo` | hidden | hidden ✅ |
| B1 | `sys_user` self, `email_verified=false` | **VISIBLE** | VISIBLE ✅ |
| B2 | `sys_user` self, `email_verified` forced `true` (15 keys set) | hidden | hidden ✅ |

**Fault direction on `properties.visible` (question 2) — fail-SOFT, observed**

| run | probe | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| H1 | `visible: "MARKER9167NOSUCHIDENT == 1"` on a `todo` task | **VISIBLE** — console: `Failed to evaluate expression: ${MARKER9167NOSUCHIDENT == 1} … is not defined` |

objectui#4807's reading — 「fail-soft 使作者门控的横幅永远显示」 — holds at this pin.

**Forced-sparse, unguarded — still `false`, still hidden**

| run | probe | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| C1 | task `in_review`, `status` stripped from the read (6 keys removed) | hidden ✅ |
| C2 | `sys_user` self, `email_verified` stripped (2 keys removed) | hidden ✅ |

Bare strings run on the legacy JS evaluator, where a missing key is `undefined` and `undefined == 'in_review'` is plain `false`. The #8990 absent-key **fault** class still does not reach this surface; the card title's attribution stays falsified.

**⛔ The struck step 2, executed literally — still harmful**

| run | probe | verdict | expected |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| D1 | `todo` task, `visible: "has(record.status) && record.status == 'in_review'"` | **VISIBLE** | hidden ❌ |
| D2 | verified user, `visible: "has(record.id) && has(record.email_verified) && …"` | **VISIBLE** | hidden ❌ |

Console on both: `Failed to evaluate expression … "has" is not a function`. Fail-soft turns that throw into a shown banner. **`c86185eb5` changed the node gate; it did not touch `properties.visible`.**

**⭐ The node-level `visibleWhen` gate — inert on 2026-08-20, live now**

| run | probe | verdict | reads as |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| E1 | `in_review` task (baseline VISIBLE) + `visibleWhen: {cel,'false'}` | hidden | the gate is **honoured** |
| E2 | `todo` task, `visible` dropped + `visibleWhen: {cel,'true'}` | VISIBLE | paired mount: the gate can SHOW, so E1 is the gate and not a dead block |
| F1 | `todo`, `visible` dropped + `visibleWhen: {cel,"record.status == 'in_review'"}` | hidden | `record` **binds** |
| F2 | `in_review`, same | VISIBLE | polarity-correct pair |
| E3 | `todo`, `visibleWhen: {cel,'true'}` **and** the authored `visible` left in place | hidden | the two gates compose as **AND** |

E3 is the operationally important one: a migration must **remove** `properties.visible`, not just add `visibleWhen` beside it.

**`has()` on the `visibleWhen`/CEL face — works, and is load-bearing**

| run | probe | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| G1 | `in_review`, `visibleWhen: has(record.status) && record.status == 'in_review'` | VISIBLE ✅ |
| G2 | same + `status` stripped (5 keys removed) | hidden ✅ — the guard holds |
| G3 | same but **unguarded** + `status` stripped (4 keys removed) | **VISIBLE** — `[object-ui] A conditional predicate failed to evaluate and was treated as its safe default (true) … Reason: [runtime] No such key: status` |
| G4 | verified user, guarded `visibleWhen`, `visible` dropped | hidden ✅ |
| G5 | unverified self, same predicate | VISIBLE ✅ |
| G6b | another user's record, same predicate (control: that page's own title) | hidden ✅ |
| I1 | `todo`, guarded `visibleWhen` only, polled every 150 ms for 8 s | never visible — **no flash** |
| I2 | polling control: unmodified `in_review` page | hidden → VISIBLE at 1414 ms — the poller does see banners |

G3 is the warning label on the whole migration: on the CEL face a missing key **is** a fault, and that face is fail-soft too — so moving a predicate to `visibleWhen` **without** `has()` re-arms exactly the bug this card feared, on a surface that previously could not have it. G4/G5/G6b also show `ctx.user` binds there (a fault on that half would have fail-softed G4 and G6b to VISIBLE; both are hidden).

### Controls, stated

- Every negative reading is paired: A1↔A2, B1↔B2, E1↔E2, F1↔F2, G1↔G2, G4↔G5↔G6b, I1↔I2.
- Every run asserts a page-render control string from **that** page. The first G6 run failed its control (it reused the other page's title) and was **discarded and re-run as G6b** rather than reported.
- Interception counters per run: `metaPatched=1` proves the metadata rewrite reached the `record:alert` node; `keysRemoved`/`keysSet` prove the payload rewrite touched real rows. A zero there would have invalidated the run.
- Banner detection is `[role="status"] / [role="alert"]` node text cross-checked against a body-text detector, demonstrated live in both directions in the same session.

### What I recommend be ruled — ⛔ not applied, and I am not asking to apply it myself

**Do not lift the strike; retire it and replace it.** Steps 2–3 as written stay wrong forever — they target `properties.visible`, whose evaluator has no `has()` and never will. What changed is that a *different* remedy became available and is now measured green:

> On both pages, move the predicate off `properties.visible` onto the component's declared `visibleWhen`, adding `has()` guards, and **delete the `visible` key** in the same edit.
>
> - `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/task-detail.page.ts:51` → `visibleWhen: "has(record.status) && record.status == 'in_review'"`
> - `packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-user.page.ts:79` → `visibleWhen: "has(record.id) && has(record.email_verified) && record.id == ctx.user.id && record.email_verified == false"`

- **Real business need — weak, and I will not inflate it.** Zero users hit this today; the detail read projects every declared column and the legacy evaluator answers the sparse case `false`, which is the correct verdict anyway.
- **Long-term soundness — strongest axis.** Removes a dialect fork instead of adding one, and is the downstream half of the maintainer's 2026-08-20 ruling 「A 让 record:alert 认 visibleWhen(推荐)」, whose upstream half has landed and whose pin this repo now carries.
- **Hard to get wrong for AI-written metadata — decisive, and it runs backwards today.** The sloppy bare `visible` happens to work; the guarded CEL form the platform teaches everywhere else throws and shows the banner forever (D1/D2). Under the migration, the declared slot is the one that works and a genuine fault is at least **loud** (G3 names the missing key).
- **Startup scope — cheap and bounded.** Two authored lines; the wire census says the whole authored surface is exactly these 2 blocks.

⚠️ Two conditions, measured rather than assumed: (a) the `visible` key must be **deleted**, not left beside the new gate (E3); (b) the `has()` guards are **mandatory** on the CEL face — unguarded there is strictly worse than today (G3).
